sections.title: Bodies, Borders, Catastrophes
sections.description:
This course investigates constructions of gender and sexuality adjacent to environmental catastrophe. We will read the fluid movements between human and nonhuman bodies to reframe our ideas of queerness and gender. We will study ecofeminist literature from the US, Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean to interrogate the sexual and racial formations that emerge around imperial violence and extraction ecologies. We will examine monstrosity, hybridity, mechanicality, and animality; we will trace how the slow and fast violences of environmental collapse degrade, fragment, and reorganize gendered bodies. How might we read the relationships between human, nonhuman, animal, and machine bodies in the context of environmental disaster? How might we understand disease and disability in relation to the global movements of resources? What might be “trans” about this
environmental interflow of bodies? As we aggregate postcolonial, indigenous, and ecofeminist literature, we will map the queer networks that interlink the diseased, fractured, and mutable bodies of climate collapse. Assignments will include class presentations, short writing exercises, and peer reviews; students may choose between a creative or critical final project.
